title: THE GREEN THEATRE (TGT) – Sustainability in Perioperative Medicine: a pre–post study to investigate the effect of an educational programme designed to increase awareness of emission-reducing measures in perioperative medicine
summary:
This project aims to assess and evaluate awareness and knowledge among healthcare staff regarding the environmental impact of perioperative medicine.
The study is based on an educational programme. Participation in this programme is expected to improve the knowledge of staff in the participating departments and to promote the implementation of environmentally sustainable measures in clinical practice. Within the study, participation in the educational programme is regarded as the intervention.
The effectiveness of the programme will be measured by means of a before-and-after survey, with a focus on potential changes in knowledge and attitudes. In addition, objective parameters such as the consumption of anaesthetic gases (determined by fresh gas flow rates) and the quality of waste separation will be examined.
The central research question is: Can an educational programme reduce emissions in perioperative medicine? Furthermore, the study aims to identify barriers that hinder CO2e-saving practices in the perioperative setting.
conditions: Examination of knowledge, attitudes, and clinical behavior of employees in the perioperative area regarding ecological sustainability in healthcare. In addition, assessment of resource-related behavior in the operating room, particularly with regard to anesthetic gas consumption (fresh gas flow) and waste separation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Nursing or medical work at University Hospital Cologne in anaesthesia or in other departments within the perioperative area (operating theatre / surgical intensive care units)
• Consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
• No consent to participate in the study
• No active employment in the above-mentioned departments of the University Hospital Cologne
